audience_note: B2B only: wholesalers, retailers, distributors, beauty/perfume store buyers sourcing product to resell. All keyword and template decisions are filtered for this ICP; consumer-intent fragrance content (notes, reviews, 'best perfumes for X') is explicitly out of scope.
prior_findings_used: Manual GSC audit (last 30 days) found ZERO wholesale-buyer-intent queries in Search Console -- top queries were brand-name confusion and specific SKUs. This confirms zero topical authority for commercial wholesale-buyer intent today; this plan is the remediation.

pillar.title: Wholesale Fragrance Buying: The Complete Guide for Retailers & Distributors
pillar.rationale: Broad head terms like 'wholesale perfume supplier' are dominated in the SERP by B2B aggregators (Alibaba, TradeKey, europages, Wholesale Central, Faire) and 20-40-year-old wholesale distributor storefronts -- not winnable via editorial content for a manufacturer site. The pillar keyword is instead an informational buyer-education phrase, matching the SERP shape (blog-style guides from Qogita, Wholesale55, DMS Retail, World Perfume) where individual company blogs -- including other wholesale fragrance businesses -- do rank. The pillar's job is topical-authority signaling and internal-link hub, not competing for the aggregator-dominated head term.
pillar.volume: not available (no Ads API access; qualitative signal: consistent 6-9 result blog-competitor set recurring across every sourcing-adjacent query tested, indicating real, sustained search demand)
pillar.build_note: New page, not a rewrite of the existing 'How Wholesale Fragrance Sourcing Actually Works' post. That post stays live as Cluster 1's lead spoke. The pillar is a new, broader overview that summarizes all 4 clusters and links out to all 13 spokes -- lower risk than expanding a live, already-indexed page.

clusters.name: Sourcing & Supplier Vetting
clusters.rationale: Deepens the existing sourcing post. SERP evidence: 'how to find a reliable wholesale perfume supplier' and 'perfume MOQ' both return blog-style advice content (Qogita, Wholesale55, DMS Retail, sunflorae, jarskingglobal) -- winnable. Contrast with 'wholesale perfume supplier' (bare head term), which returns aggregators/direct competitor storefronts and is excluded from this cluster.

posts.title: Wholesale Perfume Payment Terms: Deposits, Balances & What's Normal

clusters.name: Shipping, Customs & Logistics
clusters.rationale: Deepens the existing shipping/customs post. SERP evidence: dangerous-goods/HS-code and freight-mode queries return logistics-vertical blogs (Packamor, FreightAmigo, atoship, World Perfume), not aggregators -- a manufacturer can credibly compete here, especially with the perfume-specific flammability angle general freight blogs don't own.

posts.title: Shipping & Customs Guide for Wholesale Perfume Buyers
posts.note: Existing post. Covers ABV/flammable classification, documentation, duty variability. Serves as cluster lead.

posts.title: Why Perfume Ships as a Dangerous Good: HS Codes, UN1266 & What It Means for Your Order
posts.keyword: perfume dangerous goods shipping HS code
posts.evidence: SERP dominated by logistics-niche blogs (FreightAmigo, atoship, LAEYO Labs, Gerudo Logistics, deepbeez) covering UN1266/Class 3 classification and HS 3303 vs. 3304 misclassification risk -- specific, technical, low-competition-from-consumer-content topic that reinforces Royal Perfumes' 'we prepare accurate documentation' claim with real regulatory detail.

posts.title: Air vs. Sea Freight for Wholesale Perfume: Which Should You Choose?
posts.keyword: air freight vs sea freight perfume wholesale
posts.evidence: Validated real cost data ($800-1,400 air vs. $250-500 sea for a typical wholesale order; air freight often barred for large flammable-liquid volume). SERP is dominated by generic freight-industry sites (Freightos, Onramp Funds, Tuscor Lloyds) with no perfume-specific competitor except World Perfume -- winnable only if the post leads with the perfume/flammability-specific angle, not generic freight advice.

clusters.name: Scent-Matched / Inspired Fragrances
clusters.rationale: Deepens the existing inspired-vs-designer post. SERP evidence: both the legal-compliance angle and the smell-comparison angle are won by brand-owned blogs from other inspired-fragrance sellers (DUA Fragrances, Regal Fragrances, Noor Perfume, a direct 'Royal Perfume'-branded competitor mbroyalperfume.ca) -- direct proof that a fragrance company's own blog can rank here, and a competitive gap Royal Perfumes is not yet contesting.

posts.title: Scent-Matched Fragrances Explained: How "Inspired By" Perfumes Compare to Designer Originals
posts.note: Existing post. Covers note structure, price-gap rationale, what varies between suppliers. Serves as cluster lead.

posts.title: Is It Legal to Sell Inspired Perfumes? A Wholesale Buyer's Compliance Guide
posts.keyword: is it legal to sell perfume dupes
posts.evidence: Real, recurring buyer question -- SERP includes law-firm content (Ropes & Gray), IP blogs (Intepat), and dupe-focused retailer blogs (perfumeson, world-perfume, aromapassions, modfragrances). This is one of the single biggest hesitation points for a first-time retailer stocking inspired fragrances and is currently completely unaddressed on the site -- high priority.

posts.title: How Close Do Inspired Perfumes Really Smell to the Designer Original?

posts.evidence: 9-result SERP entirely composed of inspired-fragrance brand blogs (DUA Fragrances, mbroyalperfume.ca, bkaroma, Regal Fragrances, Noor Perfume, Valon, Elite Perfumes, Leclair & Moreau) -- zero aggregators, zero legal sites. Strongest proof point in the whole research set that brand-owned content wins this exact query type.

clusters.name: Wholesale Business Economics
clusters.rationale: New cluster, not derived from an existing post. Validated by SERP evidence that other wholesale fragrance businesses (perfumes.la ranks twice for 'how to start a perfume reselling business'; World Perfume ranks across margin, negotiation, and start-a-business queries; Wholesale55 ranks across MOQ, scam-spotting, and start-a-business queries) win exactly this content type. This is the clearest gap: none of the 3 existing posts address why/how to run a resale business, only how to buy from a supplier.

posts.title: How to Start a Fragrance Reselling Business: A Step-by-Step Guide for Retailers
posts.keyword: how to start a perfume reselling business
posts.evidence: SERP includes Shopify, BeauteTrade, Wholesale55, and perfumes.la (a direct wholesale-fragrance-business analog ranking twice) -- strongest direct proof in this entire research set that a wholesale fragrance seller's blog can win this query. This is the single highest-value new spoke: it captures buyers before they've picked a supplier.

posts.title: Wholesale Perfume Profit Margins: What Retailers Actually Make
posts.evidence: SERP includes a Turkish perfume-company blog (jasmine-perfumes.com.tr) ranking alongside business-finance sites -- direct evidence a manufacturer blog based in Turkey (Royal Perfumes' own market position) can win this. High buyer-research value: margin data is exactly what a prospective retailer needs before committing to an MOQ order.

posts.title: Dropshipping vs. Wholesale: Why Serious Fragrance Retailers Buy in Bulk
posts.evidence: SERP dominated by dropship-tool platforms (Inventory Source, Doba, AutoDS, SellTheTrend) with no bulk-manufacturer content addressing the comparison from the wholesale side -- a genuine content gap and a natural filter/qualification page that pre-sells the 500-unit MOQ economics against a lower-commitment alternative.

clusters.name: Trending Categories: Arabic & Oud Fragrances
clusters.rationale: Added 2026-09-14 from live trend research (WebSearch), not the original SERP-overlap pass. Western search interest in 'oud' is up ~20.5% YoY and 'Arabian perfume' up ~63% YoY (multiple 2026 market-trend sources), driven by niche/gender-neutral demand shift + TikTok discovery. Royal Perfumes already stocks established Arabic/oud brands (Lattafa confirmed in product catalog), making this a genuine content + inventory match rather than a speculative category bet. Unlike the other 4 clusters (process-oriented: sourcing/shipping/inspired/business), this cluster targets trending product-category intent.

posts.title: Wholesale Arabic & Oud Fragrances: What's Trending and Worth Stocking
posts.keyword: wholesale arabic perfume / oud fragrance wholesale
posts.evidence: Trend data (not SERP-overlap): oud +20.5% YoY, Arabian perfume +63% YoY Western search interest; Lattafa is one of the most-searched fragrance brands of 2026 and is already in Royal Perfumes' active catalog (e.g. lattafa-khamrah-karaz-100ml). No existing cluster covered trending product categories -- clear content gap.

posts.title: Wholesale Travel-Size & Mini Perfume: Why Retailers Are Stocking the 10ml Format
posts.keyword: travel size perfume wholesale / mini perfume wholesale
posts.evidence: Sourced from a user-supplied Google Trends export (worldwide, top + rising 'perfume'-related queries, pulled 2026-09-14): 'small perfume' shows +1750% YoY growth, one of the largest risers in the dataset. Cross-validated independently by earlier WebSearch market research noting '10ml roller and 15ml portable spray configurations emerging as preferred formats for B2B entry strategies.' Confirmed against live product catalog -- Royal Perfumes already stocks travel-set SKUs (Maison Francis Kurkdjian 5x11ml sets: 724, Grand Soir, Baccarat Rouge 540, Oud Satin Mood). Other risers from the same Trends export ('perfume for kids' +3800%, 'purple perfume' +1800%, 'sony perfume' breakout) were evaluated and explicitly excluded -- kids' fragrance has no matching catalog SKUs, and the other two have no identifiable, sourceable driver worth acting on.

excluded_or_deferred.reason: Same aggregator/competitor-dominated pattern (4-5 domain overlap with 'wholesale perfume supplier' in SERP testing) -- transactional intent better served by an optimized /shop category page than a blog post.
